title: Docetaxel for hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
context_label: Castration-sensitive prostate cancer: metastatic or selected high-risk nonmetastatic source indications
indication_text: Castration-sensitive prostate cancer: metastatic or selected high-risk nonmetastatic source indications
purpose: Add chemotherapy to the overall prostate treatment plan. Expected benefit depends on whether the disease has spread.
schedule_summary: Docetaxel 75 mg/m² is infused over one hour on Day 1 every 21 days. The team writes the planned course: NCCP 00203 does not set a six-cycle prostate cap, while CHAARTED used six cycles. Continuous prednisolone is not specified in this source.
administration_text: Dexamethasone 8 mg twice daily for three days, starting the day before docetaxel; take at least three doses before the infusion. Tell the team if any dose is missed.
monitoring_summary: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests at baseline and before each cycle. Review infection, neuropathy, fluid retention and skin/mouth toxicity before treatment.
safety_note: Call your oncology team immediately for fever, shaking chills, feeling suddenly unwell, unusual bleeding or persistent vomiting/diarrhoea. Follow your own temperature and contact plan. Severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, collapse or new leg weakness with bladder/bowel changes: call 112/999.

agents.name: Docetaxel
agents.mechanism: Docetaxel disrupts microtubules needed for cell division. It adds a different anticancer action to testosterone suppression; the disease setting determines whether adding chemotherapy is worthwhile.
agents.explanation: Docetaxel disrupts microtubules needed for cell division. It adds a different anticancer action to testosterone suppression; the disease setting determines whether adding chemotherapy is worthwhile.
risks: Low white cells: infection, neutropenic sepsis and possible death
Low red cells: fatigue or breathlessness; low platelets: bruising or bleeding
Allergic infusion reactions, occasionally severe or life-threatening
Nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation, sore mouth and reduced appetite
Tiredness, hair loss, taste changes, skin and nail effects
Nerve damage: tingling, numbness or weakness, sometimes lasting
Liver abnormalities; rare serious bowel inflammation, bleeding or perforation
Fluid retention and swelling; rare lung inflammation or serious breathing problems

items.title: Evidence in this setting
items.text: In the original CHAARTED analysis of 790 people with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, ADT plus six cycles of docetaxel gave median overall survival of 57.6 versus 44.0 months with ADT alone; hazard ratio 0.61 (95% CI 0.47–0.80), with median follow-up 28.9 months. Do not transfer this result to nonmetastatic disease: long-term STAMPEDE M0 analysis did not establish an overall-survival advantage (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.64–1.21). These are different populations and historical comparators, not a comparison with contemporary triplet treatment.

evidence.interpretation: In the original CHAARTED analysis of 790 people with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, ADT plus six cycles of docetaxel gave median overall survival of 57.6 versus 44.0 months with ADT alone; hazard ratio 0.61 (95% CI 0.47–0.80), with median follow-up 28.9 months. Do not transfer this result to nonmetastatic disease: long-term STAMPEDE M0 analysis did not establish an overall-survival advantage (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.64–1.21). These are different populations and historical comparators, not a comparison with contemporary triplet treatment.
limitations: Historical comparisons may not reflect modern previous treatment or available alternatives.
Do not extrapolate outcomes across hormone-sensitive, castration-resistant and nonmetastatic disease.
